rationales: Guttation is the loss of liquid water droplets, not water evaporated from the plant surface.
Transportation is the movement of materials within an organism.
Transpiration is the loss of water from plant surfaces by evaporation.
Transduction is the transfer of genetic material or a signal, not water loss.
Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials and are not sites of aerobic respiration.
Vacuoles mainly store materials and are not sites of aerobic respiration.
Centrioles help organize cell division and are not sites of aerobic respiration.
G-0 is a resting state outside the active cell cycle.
G-1 is a growth phase before DNA replication.
G-2 is a growth and preparation phase after DNA replication.
The S-phase is when DNA is replicated, duplicating the chromosomes.
Prophase I is the longest phase of meiosis, with several distinct stages.
Metaphase I is shorter and involves chromosome pairs lining up at the cell equator.
Anaphase I involves the separation of homologous chromosomes.
Telophase I is the concluding phase of the first meiotic division.
A co-factor assists an enzyme but is not the molecule on which it acts.
A product is formed by the enzyme-catalyzed reaction.
The molecule on which an enzyme acts is called its substrate.
A co-enzyme is an assisting organic molecule, not the enzyme’s target molecule.
Glucose is a product of photosynthesis, not its byproduct in this context.
Oxygen is released as a byproduct of photosynthesis.
Carbon dioxide is a raw material used in photosynthesis.
Water is a raw material used in photosynthesis, not the released byproduct.
Lubrication reduces friction and helps food move through the digestive tract.
Mastication is the grinding and chewing of food by the teeth.
Defecation is the elimination of feces from the body.
Absorption is the uptake of digested nutrients.
Euglena consists of a single cell, so it is not multicellular.
Euglena is a unicellular organism.
Acellular describes entities without cellular organization, such as viruses.
Colonial organisms consist of groups of associated cells, unlike single-celled Euglena.
Observations provide information but are not the basis from which scientific deductions are drawn in this sequence.
Deductions are logical consequences drawn from a hypothesis.
A theory is a well-supported explanation, not the immediate source of these deductions.
A law describes a consistent pattern, rather than serving as the source of deductions here.
Primates is an order of mammals, not pea plants.
Pisum is the genus of pea, not its order.
Plantae is a kingdom, not an order.
Fabales is the order to which the pea plant belongs.
An organelle is a structure within a cell, not a group of similar cells.
A tissue is a group of similar cells organized to perform a function.
An organ is made of different tissues working together.
An organ system is a group of organs working together.
Experiments test deductions or hypotheses rather than being the logical consequences themselves.
Observations are recorded information, not logical consequences of a hypothesis.
Deductions are logical consequences derived from a hypothesis.
Data are collected information, not the logical consequences of a hypothesis.
In the classification used here, algae are included in Kingdom Protista.
Fungi includes organisms such as molds and mushrooms, not algae.
Plantae includes plants, but algae are placed in Protista in this classification.
Animalia includes animals, not algae.
The matrix is the fluid-filled interior of a mitochondrion.
A granum is a stack of thylakoids in a chloroplast.
Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Thylakoids are membrane structures in chloroplasts.
An adult human liver does not typically weigh 2.5 kg.
An adult human liver weighs about 1.5 kg.
An adult human liver is substantially heavier than 0.5 kg.
An adult human liver does not typically weigh 5 kg.
